findings.title: alignmentLine reuse breaks loadCommitMessage's "skipped leaves message unchanged" contract
findings.detail: alignmentLine(a) now returns a non-empty string ("skipped", "N clauses awaiting confirmation", or "N clauses confirmed, verdicts pending") for states that previously produced "". internal/cli/cmd_next.go:539-552 loadCommitMessage explicitly reuses this same alignmentLine (per its own doc comment, unmodified in this diff) and relies on it returning "" whenever there are no verdict artifacts: 'No verdict artifacts (the audit is disabled, skipped, or has not run yet) leaves the message unchanged.' That contract is now broken for the reachable 'explicitly skipped' path: takt answer --gate agent_invalid --choice skip → skipAlignment(bdir, st) sets alignment.json's Skipped=true; decidePlan's ClausesPresent/ClausesConfirmed/VerdictsPresent facts all become true via the `|| a.Skipped` OR (internal/cli/facts.go:78-80), so the plan→execute transition proceeds immediately and loadCommitMessage is called with a.Skipped=true. alignmentLine now hits `case a.Skipped: return gateSkipped` and returns "skipped" (non-empty), so the commit subject/body now gets " — alignment: skipped" appended, directly contradicting the still-present, unmodified doc comment and the existing behaviour TestLoadCommitMessageOmitsAlignmentWhenAbsent pins for the 'no verdict artifacts' cases (that test only covers the fully-absent alignment.json case, not the explicit-skip case, so it does not catch this). The two other new non-empty branches ('N clauses awaiting confirmation' / 'N clauses confirmed, verdicts pending') cannot actually be reached from decidePlan's transition gate, so only the Skipped branch is a live regression, but it is a real, untested one.
